items.stem: A UI test fails intermittently because it clicks a button before the page finishes loading. What is the maintainable fix?

options.text: Replace the fixed sleep with an explicit wait for the element to be interactable
options.rationale: Correct: an explicit condition-based wait handles variable load times reliably.

options.text: Add a longer fixed sleep before the click
options.rationale: Longer sleeps slow the suite and still fail under load spikes.

options.text: Wrap the test in an automatic retry and move on
options.rationale: Retrying masks the timing defect rather than fixing it.

options.text: Delete the assertion after the click
options.rationale: Removing the assertion removes the test's value.

items.explanation: Correct: explicit waits on a condition are the reliable, maintainable answer to timing flakiness.

items.stem: Which TWO practices reduce maintenance cost when the UI changes frequently? (Select TWO)

options.text: Encapsulating each screen behind a page object
options.rationale: Correct: a page object localises UI changes to one place.

options.text: Selecting elements by stable test IDs rather than layout-dependent paths
options.rationale: Correct: stable test IDs survive layout and styling changes.

options.text: Duplicating selector strings in every test
options.rationale: Duplication multiplies the edits needed for one change.

options.text: Selecting elements by their absolute XPath position
options.rationale: Absolute XPath breaks on minor structural changes.

items.explanation: Correct: page objects and stable test IDs both confine the impact of UI changes.

items.stem: Which distribution matches a healthy test pyramid?

options.text: Many fast unit tests, fewer service tests, few UI tests
options.rationale: Correct: the pyramid favours many cheap unit tests and few expensive UI tests.

options.text: Mostly UI tests with few unit tests
options.rationale: That is the ice-cream-cone anti-pattern, which is slow and brittle.
End-to-end-only suites are slow and hard to diagnose.

options.text: Equal numbers at every level regardless of cost
options.rationale: Ignoring cost and speed defeats the purpose of the pyramid.

items.explanation: Correct: the pyramid concentrates tests at the fast, cheap unit level and minimises UI tests.
